reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes OneCoin through a network-marketing team, claims that participants can create money and achieve success, and directly urges viewers to join. His emphasis on team growth and duplication ties the recruitment pitch to the promised benefit, rather than presenting an independent report or an ordinary operational tutorial.

citations.quote: I am a top leader at OneCoin.
All the people onboard on the network, and then people who have never done network marketing.
Now WANCOIN we are ourselves the miners of money!
I assure you and join us because it is so incredible

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker grounds his account in his own experience: he says, "I have lived an incredible life with OneCoin," and describes his enthusiasm as a first for him. Those are personal assessments, not a stated promise that viewers will earn the same amount or receive a guaranteed return. His invitation is emphatic, but enthusiasm should not be treated as a financial guarantee that the video never actually gives.

citations.quote: I have lived an incredible life with OneCoin.
it is the first time in my life that I have so much enthusiasm
Come. Join us.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies an invitation and a claim about creating money. But "miners of money" does not specify an amount, a guaranteed return, or a payment for recruiting someone else. The speaker's enthusiasm may warrant skepticism; it does not, by itself, establish the particular financial promise the opening reads into it.

citations.quote: Now WANCOIN we are ourselves the miners of money!
I assure you and join us because it is so incredible

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An explicit guaranteed return is not necessary to recognize this pitch. The speaker calls himself a OneCoin leader, says newcomers can succeed, and urges the audience to join. Personal phrasing does not neutralize those claims or turn the invitation into detached lifestyle commentary.

citations.quote: I am a top leader at OneCoin.
Anyone who has never heard of cryptocurrency can succeed with ONE COIN
Come. Join us.

opening.argument: Judge, part of this interview is the speaker's view of cryptocurrency adoption. He connects OneCoin to bitcoin, recalls what he says France missed in 2009, and invokes financial institutions' interest in cryptocurrency. Read as investment commentary, those remarks express a view of a developing market, not evidence that the viewer is promised a defined payout. The interview framing also lets a viewer recognize that these are the speaker's claims, not independently verified financial facts.

citations.quote: You all have heard about cryptocurrency, bitcoins, you all know what is in the future even financial institutions say it's the future.
So we are not going to miss it, what we missed with BTC in 2009 because nobody had invested in France at least!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the discussion of bitcoin and mining as part of a recruitment promise. Yet the quoted "miners of money" line does not explain how anyone is paid, while the bitcoin comparison is a claim about an opportunity the speaker thinks was missed. Those claims may be overstated, but the cited words do not establish a commission structure.

citations.quote: Now WANCOIN we are ourselves the miners of money!
what we missed with BTC in 2009 because nobody had invested in France at least!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cryptocurrency comparison serves the invitation, not an independent market analysis. The speaker says anyone can succeed with OneCoin, emphasizes the team's growth, and ends by telling viewers to join. The absence of a commission formula limits what can be said about its precise terms, but does not erase the recruitment pitch.

citations.quote: Anyone who has never heard of cryptocurrency can succeed with ONE COIN
We are a team that has just started.
Come. Join us.

opening.argument: Judge, this can be read as a business representative promoting a service and inviting people to learn about it. The description supplies a signup link, but the supplied material does not state a required deposit, a return rate, a downline commission, or a request for credentials. The speaker's claims about simplicity and team growth are promotional; neither claim spells out the mechanism by which recruiting another person would pay the viewer. Evaluate the observed invitation without supplying missing transaction terms.

citations.quote: What I love about ONE COIN is the simplicity and the duplication.
We are a team that has just started.
https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/affiliate001
Come. Join us.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening links onboarding and duplication to a promised benefit, but its excerpts do not state that a viewer earns a commission when another person enrolls. Even "top leader" identifies the speaker's role, not a payout rule. That distinction matters when judging what this video itself establishes about the offer.

citations.quote: All the people onboard on the network, and then people who have never done network marketing.
What I love about ONE COIN is the simplicity and the duplication.
I am a top leader at OneCoin.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The pitch goes beyond a neutral description of a service: a self-described network-marketing leader stresses duplication, says newcomers can succeed, and directs viewers to join; the description provides an affiliate signup link. Those facts support a recruitment-focused reading even though the video does not disclose a commission formula. Missing terms should not be invented, but neither should they make the visible promotion disappear.
